newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended marginally lower on Friday, getting a late boost from a firm opening on Wall Street which pushed the AEX index up from an off early dip.
The index closed at 870.45 points, down 0.18 on Thursday, and still below yesterday's intra-day record peak of 875.61.
Index heavyweights Philips, Royals Dutch and KLM all ended with gains, helping to counter a general weakness elsewhere. Financials continued to lag the market.
With little corporate news around, KLM was boosted by an upgrade from analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, who increased their EPS forecasts for the company in 1997/98 and 1998/99.
The Dutch flag carrier closed 1.50 guilders higher at 61.70.
Philips continued its strong run, putting on another 2.50 guilders in relatively slack volumes to finish at 142.10, although some dealers said the stock was now looking overbought.
Akzo added a further 6.40 guilders to end at 271.80 after a 1.90 guilder gain on Thursday on the back of news that trials of its anti-depression drug Remeron had been positive.
Financials took a little shine off the index, with banks ABN AMRO losing 0.60 guilders to 36.60 and ING down 0.70 to 90.80 guilders. Insurer Aegon also underperformed, losing 1.20 guilders to 135.20.
Royal Dutch bounced off its early lows to end positively again. Its hefty 7.80 guilder gain yesterday sparked some early profit-taking but buying soon came back into the stock.

The initial gains were sparked by firming energy prices after OPEC's agreement to commit to oil quotas. Dealers said the gains were linked to the oil giant's 4-for-1 stock split which is due to take effect from Monday and had encouraged investor accumulation this week.
